budget_items.topic: Health insurance rate increase with no plan changes
budget_items.what_was_recorded: Without plan changes, health insurance rates would rise 6.82%, effective July 1, 2018.
budget_items.quote: if there are no changes to the plan, there would be a 6.82% increase in rates.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Specialist, emergency room, outpatient surgery and CAT scan copayments under the current plan were described.
budget_items.quote: specialists are a flat $25 copayment. an emergency room visit is a $100 copayment.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: The plan design would add a calendar deductible of $250 per person, capped at $750 per family.
budget_items.quote: basically the town would be adding a calendar deductible of $250/person and capped at $750 per family.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Under the GIC benchmark plan, the primary care flat fee would be $20.00 and specialist visits would rise from $25 to $35.
budget_items.quote: the flat fee is $20.00 visit. specialist office visits would go from $25 to $35.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Hospital admissions under the benchmark plan would be $300/$700 after the deductible is satisfied.
budget_items.quote: hospital admissions would go to $300/$700 after the deductible is satisfied.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Keeping the $200/$400 hospital copayment would add 0.2 percent to premium rates, a total 3.61 percent increase.
budget_items.quote: that is a possibility and it would add .2 percent to the premium rates. we would be looking at a 3.61 percent increase.

budget_items.topic: Retiree Medicare Part B premium reimbursement
budget_items.what_was_recorded: The Town pays 75% of the Medicare Part B premium, averaging $135/month per enrolled retiree and spouse; the presenter said this is becoming uncommon and should be addressed in negotiations.
budget_items.quote: currently the town is paying 75% of the medicare part b premium which on average is $135/month for every enrolled retiree and spouse.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: The presenter recommended working with an actuary to reduce the OPEB liability; no dollar figure was printed.
budget_items.quote: ms. shillue recommended working with an actuary to reduce the opeb liability.
